defect_summary: governance/router.py had 19 route handlers that call the local _identity(authorization) closure and discard the return value, so they could not capability-gate their response content. BFF-REVIEW-QUEUE-REDACTION-REPAIR-001 fixed the review-queue endpoints and its own evidence file flagged GET /bff/management/governance-ledger as a newly discovered, out-of-scope gap (governance_ledger() aggregates evidence_refs from approval_queue/approval_decisions/interventions/audit_events without ever redacting). This task audits all 19 discarded-identity handlers, redacts the 11 whose response actually carries evidence_refs (including the ledger), and documents why the remaining 8 carry no capability-gated content.

implementation_note_governance_ledger: GovernanceService.governance_ledger() (service.py) does not accept an identity/capabilities argument. Rather than threading identity through the service layer (which would touch governance/service.py and diverge from every other already-correct handler's pattern of redacting the assembled response in the router), the router now redacts response["data"]["items"] post-hoc with the same _redact_evidence_field_items() helper used elsewhere, after the service call and after the service's own pagination. This keeps the diff scoped to governance/router.py + the new test file and inventory registration -- service.py, human_inbox.py, models.py, auth/policy.py, core/app_factory.py, and management_read_models/service.py are all unchanged, matching the precedent set by BFF-REVIEW-QUEUE-REDACTION-REPAIR-001. Flagging for reviewer preference: pushing this into the service layer (for symmetry with consult_memo_projection/mutation_review_projection, which redact inside service.py) is a viable alternative if a future task wants ledger-source-level redaction instead of response-shape redaction.
governance_ledger_dedup_note: governance_ledger() keys entries by f"ledger-approval-{decision_id}" via dict.setdefault, so when the same decision_id appears in both approval_queue_items and approval_decisions, only the first-seen (queue-sourced) entry survives in the ledger; the decisions-sourced entry for that id is dropped. This is pre-existing service.py behavior, not introduced or changed by this task. Regression coverage in test_governance_evidence_redaction_sweep.py is written against this actual dedup behavior (one approval-queue-sourced entry, one intervention entry, two audit entries) rather than four independently-observable per-id ledger rows.
fix_summary: services/control-plane/bff/governance/router.py: added two shared redaction helpers inside create_governance_router() alongside the existing _safe_redact/_redact_review_queue_items from BFF-REVIEW-QUEUE-REDACTION-REPAIR-001: _redact_evidence_field_items(identity, items, field="evidence_refs") for flat lists of dicts carrying a top-level evidence-ref list (approval decisions/queue, audit events, ledger entries, transcript events), and _redact_consultation_metadata_evidence(identity, items) for session-shaped dicts carrying metadata.consultation.evidence_refs (consultation session/participants/outcome). Fixed the 11 handlers above: each now assigns identity = _identity(authorization) (previously discarded) and routes its evidence-bearing payload through one of the two helpers -- always after any pagination/page-slicing has already happened, so redacted_evidence_count covers only the returned page. Every withheld ref carries redacted:true, required_capability, reason="insufficient_capability" (BFF-FINAL-007 shape, produced by the pre-existing, unchanged models.redact_evidence_refs/RedactedEvidenceRef). Fails closed: _safe_redact (unchanged) substitutes an empty capability set on any capability-lookup failure, so every capability-gated ref is withheld rather than disclosed. The 8 no-op handlers were left discarding identity, each with a documented reason above for why their response carries no capability-gated content. No changes to models.py, auth/policy.py, core/app_factory.py, governance/service.py, governance/human_inbox.py, or management_read_models/service.py -- the canonical redaction policy owner and its wiring were already correct; only router.py needed the missing calls.

regression_coverage_added.harness: Builds the real create_governance_router() directly (never imports main), wired exactly like core/app_factory.py: redact_evidence_refs=models.redact_evidence_refs, capabilities_for_identity=auth.policy.capabilities_for_identity, extract_identity=auth.policy.extract_identity. No class-level monkeypatching of domain services -- a minimal read-store double (_SweepStore) supplies fixture rows with mixed alert/metric/job evidence_refs.
coverage: Every one of the 11 fixed handlers exercised with a low-capability identity (operator role: holds risk.alert.read, lacks metric.read and job.read) asserting the metric/job refs are withheld (redacted:true, required_capability, reason=insufficient_capability) while the alert ref passes through, and the correct redacted_evidence_count is reported.
Every fixed handler also exercised with a full-capability identity (admin role) asserting nothing is redacted.
list_governance_approval_queue paginated across two pages (page_size=1) asserting redacted_evidence_count reflects only the item on the returned page, not the full unpaginated set.

Fail-closed coverage for get_approval_decision_detail, bff_management_governance_ledger, and get_consultation_participants: capabilities_for_identity raising -> every capability-gated ref withheld even for an identity that would otherwise have full capabilities.

bff_management_governance_ledger coverage across all four evidence sources feeding the ledger (approval_queue_items, approval_decisions -- subject to the dedup behavior noted above, v5_interventions, governance_audit_events).
